rationale: Ranking supported contracts by distance from the quoted midpoint produces a top 50 whose median quoted width is 0.240 against 0.030 for the supported set as a whole, with 17 of 50 having the model price inside the spread. The claim under test is that this is a structural property of the exchange, not a quirk of one snapshot: apparent model-market disagreement is generated by illiquidity.
features: quote width, open interest, volume, minutes_since_price_change at snapshot time
target: correlation between |model - mid| and quoted width across snapshots, and the realised settlement performance of wide-book contracts
expected_direction: The correlation persists across every 2026 snapshot, and contracts selected on midpoint distance show no better realised calibration than contracts selected at random from the same families.
test_plan: Prospective across all 2026 snapshots. Pre-specified: report the width/disagreement correlation per snapshot, and at season end compare realised Brier of the top-50-by-midpoint-distance set against a width-matched random control from the same families. Correcting for multiplicity across families with Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.10.
notes: This is registered as the platform's standing guard against the wide-spread trap. If it is confirmed, no selection rule based on midpoint distance may ever be used to build a card.
